1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: You (plural) put forward, send ahead, or advance (something) — to send something on ahead of oneself, especially good deeds laid up for the future.
5.grammar: A present/imperfect verb addressed to a group of males. The tu- prefix marks 'you', and the -ū subject-ending (here shortened from -ūna) makes it plural ('you all'). The dropped final -n and the silent alif show the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive after a governing particle (e.g. 'that you send forward', 'whatever you send forward'). The doubled middle root letter (form II) gives a causative, deliberate sense: 'put forward'.
5.root: ق-د-م (q-d-m) — to precede, go ahead, advance

6.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
6.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
6.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

7.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

8.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
8.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

9.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and His Messenger' — referring to one who is sent, an envoy or apostle bearing a message, joined by 'and' and possessed by 'His.'
9.grammar: 'Messenger' joined by wa- ('and') and followed by the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here because the word is linked in possession ('Messenger OF Him'); the pronoun takes the -hi form (with i-vowel) when it follows an i-sound.
9.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one who is sent

10.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'guard yourselves / be mindful and on your guard.' The verb conveys taqwā — protecting oneself by being conscious of Allah and shielding oneself from wrongdoing and its consequences.
10.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you (all).' The -ū ending marks the masculine plural addressees ('you all'). The pattern (form VIII, from waqā 'to protect') gives the sense of taking protective care for oneself.
10.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

12.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
12.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
13.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

14.meaning: All-Hearing / ever-hearing — one who hears completely and perfectly, missing nothing of what is uttered or whispered; an intensive form stressing the fullness of the quality. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a constant, perfect quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is all-hearing").

15.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
15.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

7.meaning: 'Above / over / on top of.' An adverb of place meaning the higher position relative to something else; it can also mean 'superior to' or 'beyond.'
7.grammar: An adverb of place that is normally attached to a following noun ('above …'). Its fixed -a ending is the form such place-words take when they govern the noun that follows them.

9.meaning: The Prophet — a person who receives revelation from Allah and announces it, one given prophetic news and inspired tidings from the unseen.
9.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article 'the'. The final -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive chain, follows a preposition, or marks agreement with a preceding genitive word. The article's l assimilates into the following n (an-nabiy), since n is a 'sun letter'.

10.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
10.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

12.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
12.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

13.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with/by the saying' or 'with the word/statement'. It combines the preposition 'bi-' (with, by means of) with 'al-qawl', a verbal noun meaning an act of speech, an utterance, a statement, or a word that is spoken.
13.grammar: A preposition ('bi-', with/by) attached to a definite noun. The preposition forces the genitive case, which is why the noun ends in '-i' rather than '-u'. The '-i' ending here is the mark of a noun governed by a preposition, conveying the sense 'with the saying' or 'by means of the word'.
13.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

16.meaning: A phrase meaning 'to some' or 'for another part'. It marks the recipient or counterpart in a reciprocal pairing, the 'other side' that 'some of you' relate to.
16.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') attached to the noun 'a part/some'. The -in ending is genitive with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'): the genitive case is required after the preposition, and the tanwīn marks the noun as indefinite ('a part', not 'the part').

17.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
17.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

19.meaning: 'Your deeds / your works / your actions' — the plural of 'deed, action, work' joined to 'your' (plural).
19.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the attached possessive '-kum' ('your', referring to a group). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('your deeds [are] …').
19.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, to work; deed, action

20.meaning: And you / while you (all) — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (masculine plural), often introducing an accompanying circumstance ('while you …').
20.grammar: The conjunction wa- joined to the detached subject pronoun 'you all' (masculine). This standalone pronoun stands as a subject or for emphasis; it has a fixed form and does not change for case. With wa- it can mark a simultaneous state ('and you / while you').

22.meaning: 'You (all) perceive / sense / are aware' — to notice or become conscious of something through feeling or insight.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a group: the 'ta-' prefix means 'you' and the '-ūna' ending marks the plural 'you all' in the basic indicative ('you do / are doing'). It describes ongoing or general awareness.
22.root: ش-ع-ر (sh-ʿ-r) — to perceive, sense, be aware

6.meaning: Messenger / envoy: one who is sent bearing a message; an emissary commissioned to convey and deliver on behalf of the sender.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
11.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

12.meaning: 'Their hearts.' The noun denotes the heart as the inner seat of feeling, understanding, and intention; its very name evokes turning and fluctuation, since the heart is what shifts and changes.
12.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') with the attached possessive -hum ('their'). The -a vowel on the noun is the accusative ending, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
12.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over, change; hence the heart, which turns

13.meaning: A phrase meaning 'to / for godliness' — taqwā being the deep, protective God-consciousness that makes one wary of wrongdoing and careful to do right, as if shielding oneself from Allah's displeasure.
13.grammar: The prefix li- is a preposition ('to', 'for'). It is followed by the noun with its definite article al- ('the'), whose 'l' merges with the noun's initial 't' ('at-taqwā'); the doubling shows in 'li-ttaqwā'. The word ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case.
13.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself; wariness, mindful piety

14.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
14.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

15.meaning: Forgiveness — Allah's covering over and pardoning of sins; the act and gift of having one's faults effaced.
15.grammar: A verbal noun of the 'mafʿila' pattern, naming the abstract action of forgiving. The '-tun' ending combines the feminine '-t-' with '-un', the nominative-indefinite marker, which typically marks an indefinite subject ('a forgiveness') — the one acting or being asserted to exist.

16.meaning: 'And a reward / recompense / wage' — payment or recompense earned for one's work or deeds, joined by 'and'.
16.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a reward') preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The -un ending is indefinite ('a/an') and nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for something being introduced/named.

17.meaning: Great, immense, mighty — vast in magnitude or importance. Describes something tremendous, whether in size, weight, or gravity.
17.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern, conveying a strong, established quality. The '-un' ending marks it nominative and indefinite; as an adjective it typically agrees with and describes an indefinite noun ('a great …').

1.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
1.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

2.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
2.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

3.meaning: 'They were patient / they endured steadfastly / they persevered.' The verb means to restrain oneself, to bear hardship with calm endurance, to hold firm and not give way to panic or complaint. Ṣabr is steadfast, self-controlled perseverance.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb (Form I) in the masculine plural 'they' person. The stem ṣabar- carries the completed-action (past) sense. The -ū ending marks the doers as 'they' (masculine plural) who performed the act ('they were patient / they endured'). The written alif after it is a silent spelling convention that regularly follows the plural -ū on a verb and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
4.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

5.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

6.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
6.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
6.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: 'Surely it would have been / it certainly was' — the verb 'to be' (past tense) carrying an emphatic 'surely', often introducing the result of a hypothetical condition.

parts.en: it was / it would have been

7.grammar: The past-tense verb kāna ('was/were'), third-person masculine singular, with the emphatic prefix la- ('surely'). In conditional sentences this combination commonly heads the consequence clause ('then it surely would have been…'). The verb kāna typically takes a following predicate in the accusative describing the subject's state.
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

8.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
8.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.

9.meaning: 'For them / to them / theirs' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the pronoun 'them,' expressing that something pertains, belongs, or is owed to that group.
9.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to'), whose vowel becomes -a before an attached pronoun, joined to -hum ('them'). It commonly expresses possession or benefit — 'theirs / for them.' Particles like this carry no case or tense of their own.

10.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
10.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
10.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

11.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
11.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.

12.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
12.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
4.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

5.meaning: "he/it came to you" — a past verb "came" with the pronoun "you" as the one reached, i.e. something arrived at or reached a group of people.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base third-person masculine singular form ("he/it came"), with no extra subject suffix. The verb "to come" is intransitive, so the attached -kum is not a direct object but an indirect (dative) pronoun — "to you" (masculine plural), equivalent to "came to you (all)."

6.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

7.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

8.meaning: An imperative addressed to a group: 'seek clarity, ascertain the truth, verify carefully before acting.' It commands one to make a matter plain and certain rather than acting on assumption.
8.grammar: A Form V command verb. The connecting prefix 'fa' links it to what precedes ('so/then'). The '-ū' ending marks a command directed at a group of males (or a mixed group): 'you all, do this.'

9.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
9.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

10.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

11.meaning: 'A people, a folk, a community' — a group of human beings bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared standing.
11.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action.
11.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group, people

12.meaning: 'Out of / in ignorance' — the preposition bi- ('with/by/in') joined to jahāla, the state of not knowing, foolishness, or acting without knowledge; conveys doing something through ignorance.
12.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/in/by'), here conveying the manner 'out of ignorance.' The -in ending is the genitive case with indefinite (tanwīn) 'n' — the form a noun takes after a preposition.
12.root: ج-ه-ل (j-h-l) — to be ignorant, not know; foolishness

13.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

14.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
14.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

15.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
15.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

16.meaning: "you did / you committed" — a past-tense act attributed to a group addressed as "you." The verb faʿala means to do, act, or carry out a deed.
16.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The suffix -tum marks the subject as "you," a group of two or more (masculine plural), so it means "you (all) did."
16.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — to do, act, make, carry out a deed

17.meaning: Regretful, remorseful; those who feel sorrow and remorse over what they have done. An active participle naming the ones characterised by regret.
17.grammar: An active participle (the one doing/feeling the act) in the masculine plural. The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative or genitive state — the form used when the group is an object, follows a preposition, or serves as a predicate after certain verbs of becoming.

1.meaning: And know! — the connector 'and' joined to a command to know, realize, or be aware of something. A direct summons to a group to take firm notice.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb directed at a group. The ending -ū marks the masculine plural addressee ('you all, know!'). Prefixed with wa- ('and').

2.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
2.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

3.meaning: Among you / in you: locates something within a group of people addressed in the plural.
3.grammar: A preposition 'in/among' with an attached pronoun -kum meaning 'you' for a group of males (or mixed group). Words after the preposition fī stand in the genitive, which is why the pronoun takes this object form. The whole expresses presence or location within the addressed group.

4.meaning: 'Messenger / envoy' — one who is sent with a message. In religious usage it denotes a prophet entrusted by Allah to convey His revelation to people.
4.grammar: A noun. The final -a is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb, or — as often with this word — standing in apposition (an explanatory restatement) to another accusative noun before it.
4.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; hence a messenger/envoy

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
6.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

7.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: Much, many, abundant, numerous. An adjective describing a large quantity or great amount of something.
9.grammar: An indefinite adjective/noun. The -in ending (tanwīn with kasra) marks the genitive case together with indefiniteness ('much / of much'). The genitive is the case used after a preposition or when the word follows another noun in an 'of' relationship.
9.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

10.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
10.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

11.meaning: The matter, affair, command, or decision — either a thing being dealt with or an authoritative order that is issued. The definite article marks it as a specific, known matter.
11.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links it to a preceding noun ('… of the matter') or follows a preposition.
11.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; a matter or affair

12.meaning: surely you would be in difficulty

parts.en: surely you would be in difficulty

12.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

13.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
13.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
14.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

15.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

16.meaning: To you / towards you — directing an action or motion at the addressees.
16.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to/towards' with the attached pronoun -kum ('you all'). The pronoun takes the helping vowel -u (kumu) when followed by a word beginning with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation; it does not change the meaning.

17.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

18.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

19.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
19.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

20.meaning: Your hearts — the inner seat of feeling, intention, and understanding, belonging to a group of people.
20.grammar: A plural noun 'hearts' carrying the -i (genitive) ending because it is the first term of a possessive (iḍāfa) construction with the following pronoun -kum ('your', for a group). This noun-plus-pronoun pairing expresses possession: 'the hearts OF you all' = 'your hearts'. In Arabic the heart is understood as the center of both emotion and thought.
20.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, change

21.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

22.meaning: To you / towards you — directing an action or motion at the addressees.
22.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to/towards' with the attached pronoun -kum ('you all'). The pronoun takes the helping vowel -u (kumu) when followed by a word beginning with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation; it does not change the meaning.

23.meaning: 'Disbelief / rejection' — the act of refusing faith, denying the truth, and being ungrateful toward Allah and His signs; the opposite of belief.
23.grammar: al- is the definite article 'the'. The noun kufr ('disbelief') carries an -a ending, the accusative case, which typically marks the direct object of a verb ('… perceived/found THE disbelief').
23.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover up, to reject faith, to be ungrateful

24.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

25.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

26.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
26.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

27.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
27.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

28.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

1.meaning: Bounty, grace, favour, or abundance; something good given freely and beyond what is owed. It can mean material provision (such as profit from trade) or divine grace and excess generosity.
1.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -an (accusative case with nunation) typically marks it as the direct object of a verb ('seeking a bounty') or as the goal of an action. The nunation also makes it indefinite ('a bounty / some favour').
1.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — to be in excess, to surpass; hence grace, bounty, superiority

2.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
2.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

5.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
5.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
5.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

6.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
6.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

7.meaning: All-Wise: possessing perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right place with flawless knowledge, judgment, and purpose. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's consummate wisdom.
7.grammar: A masculine singular adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, settled quality of wisdom. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case used for a subject or, very often, a predicate describing the doer ('[He is] All-Wise').
7.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to be wise

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

3.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
3.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

4.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
4.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

5.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

6.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

7.meaning: Between the two of them — the space or relation lying amid a pair.
7.grammar: An adverb of place, 'between,' fixed in the accusative as adverbs of place commonly are; the -a marks its adverbial function ('in the place that is between'). The attached -humā is the dual pronoun 'the two of them' (exactly two).
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction; that which lies between

8.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
8.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

9.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

10.meaning: One of the two (feminine) — 'one' in its feminine form, paired with an attached pronoun 'of the two of them', so it singles out a single female from a pair. Built on the feminine of 'one' (iḥdā, counterpart of aḥad).
10.grammar: A feminine numeral 'one' in a possessive construction. The attached pronoun -humā means 'the two of them' (a dual 'them'), so the whole expresses 'one (female) of the two of them'. The -ā of iḥdā is part of the fixed feminine form, not a case vowel.
10.root: ا-ح-د (ʾ-ḥ-d) — oneness, unity; a single one

11.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
11.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
11.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

12.meaning: The other (feminine) — the remaining or second one of two, in its feminine form. It denotes 'the other female' as opposed to the one already mentioned. Feminine of ākhar.
12.grammar: A definite feminine adjective/noun meaning 'the other'. The final -ā is the fixed feminine ending of this elative pattern (fuʿlā), which does not change for case — so no separate case vowel is added. It pairs with masculine al-ākhar.
12.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, other, coming after

13.meaning: A command 'so fight!' addressed to a group — engage in battle against an opponent. The pattern conveys mutual combat. The prefixed 'fa-' means 'so / then', drawing a consequence from what precedes.
13.grammar: 'So/then' joined to a command (imperative) verb in the mutual-action pattern (fā'ala). The -ū ending directs the command at a masculine-plural 'you (all)'. The silent alif after -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.

14.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
14.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

15.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

16.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
16.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

17.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

18.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
18.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

19.meaning: Command / matter / affair — an authoritative order, or more broadly a matter, decree, or business at hand. The exact sense ranges from a direct 'command' to a general 'affair'.
19.grammar: A singular noun. The final -i marks the genitive case: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …') — e.g. 'the command of …' — or follows a preposition.
19.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; also 'amr' as a matter/affair

20.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
20.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

21.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
21.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

23.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

24.meaning: Between the two of them — the space or relation lying amid a pair.
24.grammar: An adverb of place, 'between,' fixed in the accusative as adverbs of place commonly are; the -a marks its adverbial function ('in the place that is between'). The attached -humā is the dual pronoun 'the two of them' (exactly two).
24.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction; that which lies between

25.meaning: The noun 'justice / fairness / equity' introduced by the preposition 'with/in', giving the sense 'with justice' or 'in fairness' — acting in a balanced, even-handed manner.
25.grammar: A preposition 'bi-' plus the definite noun 'al-ʿadl'. The -i ending is genitive, which is required after the preposition; the whole phrase functions adverbially ('with/in justice').
25.root: ع-د-ل (ʿ-d-l) — justice, fairness, balance, setting straight

26.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

27.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
27.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

28.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
28.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

29.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
29.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
29.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

30.meaning: A noun (plural) meaning 'those who act justly / the equitable ones' — people who deal fairly and give everyone their due, establishing balance and justice. The form names them as doers of just dealing.

parts.en: one who acts justly (form IV agent)

30.grammar: A doer-noun (active participle, form IV — 'one who deals equitably') with the definite article 'al-,' made plural with the -īna ending. The -īna marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive case — the form used when the noun is a direct object or follows a preposition, as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject.

1.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
1.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

2.meaning: The believers — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm the truth and give it their security and assent.
2.grammar: A definite noun, the active participle of form IV ('mu'min,' 'one who believes/grants security'). The plural ending '-ūna' marks a masculine human plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or doer ('the believers' as those performing the action).

3.meaning: Siblings; the plural of 'brother', denoting a group of brothers (or brothers and sisters together). It is the broken (irregular) plural used for kin, conveying more than two siblings of shared parentage.
3.grammar: A plural noun marked indefinite ('siblings / some brothers'). The word ends in a tā-marbūṭa (the -a/-at of اِخۡوَة), which belongs to the stem; the inflection added on top is the tanwīn -un. That -un signals two things at once: the -u marks the nominative case (typically the doer or subject of a sentence), and the -n shows the word is indefinite, i.e. 'some siblings' rather than 'the siblings'.

4.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

5.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
5.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
5.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

6.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

7.meaning: Be mindful and wary of — guard yourselves by placing a protective barrier between yourselves and harm or wrongdoing. This is the verb of taqwā: God-conscious caution that shields one from what is forbidden.
7.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group ('you all'). The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural 'you.' Built on a reflexive pattern (Form VIII), it conveys 'protect yourselves / be on guard.'

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
